summary: A kitchen shaped around everyday life in a Prague apartment.
statement: A place for cooking, gathering and the small routines of home.
paragraph1: We approach the kitchen as part of the whole apartment: considering movement, storage and the relationship between the working area and the rest of the room.
paragraph2: Cabinet proportions, worktop space and appliance positions are considered together. The finished palette is selected with the client, from the first samples to the final hardware.
title: Vinohrady Kitchen

design_details.title: Framed cabinetry
design_details.description: Walnut-toned fronts create a continuous furniture wall. The framed doors and long brass-coloured pulls give the composition its rhythm.

design_details.title: Stone island
design_details.description: A pale, softly rounded worktop brings the preparation area into the centre of the room. The curved ends soften the passage around the island.

design_details.title: Cooking niche
design_details.description: The light stone recess creates a distinct cooking area within the darker cabinetry. Worktop, splashback and hood are read as one composition.

design_details.title: Suggested palette
design_details.description: Walnut brown · warm ivory · pale stone · brushed brass

summary: Made-to-measure storage that belongs to the room.
statement: A quieter room begins with a place for everything.
paragraph1: A wardrobe should work with the architecture rather than feel like an addition. The design considers the room’s proportions, door clearances and the way storage is used each day.
paragraph2: Inside, hanging space, shelving and drawers can be arranged around personal routines. Fronts, handles and finishes are selected as one coherent composition.
title: Smíchov Wardrobe

design_details.title: Architectural fronts
design_details.description: Tall, warm greige doors echo the room’s classical proportions. Repeated arched panels give the full-height wardrobe a quiet decorative structure.

design_details.title: Cornice & plinth
design_details.description: The upper cornice and recessed base help the joinery read as part of the architecture. Their proportions are developed with the surrounding mouldings.

design_details.title: Handles & storage
design_details.description: Paired brass-coloured pulls define the opening points. The internal arrangement can combine hanging space, adjustable shelves and drawers.

design_details.title: Suggested palette
design_details.description: Warm greige · brushed brass · natural parquet · soft ivory

summary: A considered kitchen with space to cook and gather.
statement: Practical details, brought together in one clear composition.
paragraph1: The starting point is how people move through the room: preparing food, sharing a meal and moving between the kitchen and the living space.
paragraph2: Storage and work surfaces are planned together with lighting and appliance integration. Material choices are developed through samples and a detailed proposal.
title: Žižkov Kitchen

design_details.title: Flat-front cabinetry
design_details.description: Muted plum fronts give the kitchen a deep, restrained colour. Flat panels and narrow shadow gaps keep the cabinet composition clear.

design_details.title: Stone island
design_details.description: A pale stone-toned island combines the working surface with a place to gather. Its waterfall sides and curved edge are explored in the detail studies.

design_details.title: Backsplash & lighting
design_details.description: A brushed-metal splashback reflects the room’s daylight. The slim linear pendant creates a second horizontal line over the island.

design_details.title: Suggested palette
design_details.description: Muted plum · pale stone · brushed steel · warm white

summary: A fitted library for books, objects and everyday living.
statement: Storage that gives the room its rhythm.
paragraph1: The library combines practical storage with space to display books and objects. Its proportions are considered in relation to the surrounding room and the furniture within it.
paragraph2: Shelf spacing, closed storage and display areas are developed around what needs to be kept. Finish samples help establish the right relationship between the joinery and the interior.
title: Holešovice Library

design_details.title: Library framework
design_details.description: Dark timber-toned shelving follows the room’s height. Vertical pilasters and a continuous cornice organise the wall into distinct bays.

design_details.title: Open & closed storage
design_details.description: The open shelves display books and objects, while the lower cabinets conceal everyday storage. Their lines align within the same framework.

design_details.title: Joinery details
design_details.description: Shelf divisions, door panels and brass-coloured pulls are developed as one family of details. The close-ups explore their visual relationships.

design_details.title: Suggested palette
design_details.description: Dark-stained timber · aged brass · warm plaster · beige textile

summary: A bespoke kitchen designed as part of an open living space.
statement: One room, with space for different ways of living.
paragraph1: The kitchen is considered together with its surrounding space. Working areas, circulation and the view from the living room all inform the arrangement.
paragraph2: Cabinetry, worktops and integrated storage are developed as a whole. The final materials and fittings are specified individually during the design process.
title: Brno Kitchen

design_details.title: Oak-toned island
design_details.description: Horizontal timber grain and broad drawer fronts establish the island’s calm character. The light worktop rounds around the end of the cabinetry.

design_details.title: Tall appliance bank
design_details.description: The darker full-height cabinets frame an open coffee niche. Concealed warm lighting separates the working recess from the surrounding doors.

design_details.title: Everyday working space
design_details.description: The island and window-side run provide complementary work surfaces. Narrow reveals and restrained hardware keep the focus on the materials.

design_details.title: Suggested palette
design_details.description: Light oak · warm stone · charcoal timber · taupe · warm LED

summary: A personal space for focused work and a growing collection.
statement: A room to think, read and make space for ideas.
paragraph1: A home study needs to balance a useful working surface with storage and a sense of calm. The design considers daylight, circulation and the relationship between open and closed shelving.
paragraph2: Storage dimensions and the working layout are tailored to the room. Finishes and details are chosen through the same sample-led process as every made-to-measure piece.
title: Dejvice Study

design_details.title: Built-in composition
design_details.description: Walnut-toned tall cabinets frame a pale working surface. Open shelves and a glazed display cabinet keep the centre of the composition visually light.

design_details.title: Illuminated shelves
design_details.description: Warm concealed lighting beneath the shelves brings focus to the desk and displayed objects. The cutaway study explores a recessed LED position.

design_details.title: Desk & drawers
design_details.description: A slim drawer unit sits below the continuous top. The relationship between desk edge, drawer fronts and neighbouring cabinets is developed together.

design_details.title: Suggested palette
design_details.description: Walnut brown · pale stone · warm grey · dark leather · warm LED
